findings.who: A married-filing-jointly filer whose spouse, not the filer answering, worked as a server or bartender for an employer and received qualified tips.
findings.why_no: The gate says only 'you' and 'your tips'; the filer reads it as asking only about the filer's own jobs and answers no for the spouse's employer.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 101: 'You (and/or your spouse if filing a joint return) received qualified tips in 2025'; p. 104: 'If you and/or your spouse received qualified tips as employees with respect to employment with more than one employer...'
findings.fix: Add 'you or your spouse' to the gate and make the gated tips question ask for the spouse's employer tips too.

findings.who: A filer whose occupation is on the IRS list but is not named in the gate's short examples or help, such as a dishwasher, restaurant host, concierge, maid or home cleaner, nanny, tutor, massage therapist, tattoo artist, golf caddy, tour guide, parking valet, delivery worker, or mover.
findings.why_no: They read the examples ('such as server, bartender, cook, hairdresser or driver' plus housekeepers, desk clerks, barbers) as the list, or their job title does not match an occupation title, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 103 lists dishwashers (108), host staff (109), concierges (302), maids and housekeeping cleaners (304), home cleaning service workers (407), personal care workers (501), tutors (507), nannies and babysitters (508), massage therapists (602), tattoo artists (609), golf caddies (701), tour guides (704), parking and valet attendants (801), goods delivery people (804), and home movers (809).
findings.fix: Make clear the examples are not exhaustive and the test is the occupation's duties, not the employer's job title; require checking the IRS list or add a broader 'any occupation listed at IRS.gov/TippedOccupations' confirmation.

findings.who: A filer with tips from one employer for both a listed occupation, such as server, and an unlisted occupation, such as manager or office work; or a working manager who also waits tables and receives tips for serving.
findings.why_no: They read 'not manager' and the help's 'If none of the work...' as excluding them because part of their work is unlisted, and answer no instead of applying the gate's 'any'.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 103: 'If you received tips as an employee in more than one occupation for the same employer, only those tips that were received in an occupation on the list ... are considered qualified tips. Do not include tips received in occupations that are not included on this list...'
findings.fix: Say: 'Answer yes if any of these tips were for duties in a listed occupation, even if other duties for the same employer are not listed; a later question handles the mixed work.' Do not let 'not manager' override listed duties.

findings.who: A server, bartender, or other listed-occupation employee whose employer's reported 'tips' include an automatic service charge or gratuity, or noncash tips such as tickets or meals; the filer knows those amounts are not qualified tips.
findings.why_no: They read the gate as asking whether these are qualified tips rather than whether the occupation is listed, so they answer no because the amounts are service charges or noncash, not tips.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 102: 'service charges, automatic gratuities, or any other mandatory amounts automatically added ... are not qualified tips'; 'Cash tips don't include items paid in any medium other than cash' including event tickets, meals, services, or other assets.
findings.fix: Make the gate explicitly about occupation even if some amounts are service charges or noncash; say 'Answer yes if your occupation is listed; a later question will identify nonqualified service charges or noncash amounts and may end the interview.'

Do not include tips received in occupations that are not included on this list in line 4a, 4b, or 4c"
